accepted_by_design.note: Doubt: this is the documented 2.6.1 capability-URL design (DirectDelivery), not an accident. The URL is not exposed to visitors or other members through REST lists, feed, Explore HTML, pages or og tags, and the signed /serve route refuses (no token 400, tampered 403, uid=0 og URL 403). curl with no cookies returns 200 for the current file URL of a private or followers item; the old URL after tightening returns 404.

Album privacy inheritance is the 2.6.0 design and the Edit modal explains it. POST /albums/{id}/items flips a private item to public with 200, and PUT /media/{id} {privacy:private} on an album member returns 200 with privacy still public; the REST API gives no signal. Consequence: the runbook fixture 'public album with one public and one private item' cannot be built.
File removal is deliberately asynchronous (StorageCleanupService via Action Scheduler). DB rows go at once; files stay on disk and the direct URL answers 200 until the queue runs (then 404).
WordPress core treats ?s= on a page as a native search. /media/?s= redirects to ?q= and works; /explore-media/?s=nature returns HTTP 404 with the theme 'Oops!' page.
A story is stored as ordinary public media (is_story meta) and appears in Explore and stays after expiry. Accepted: the story flow offers 'Also share as a story'.
A visitor gets 403 (members-only item shows a Log in CTA, followers item 403 with empty body) while a non-follower member gets 404 for the same followers item.
[mvs_stats] and [mvs_usage_history] return 0 bytes for a logged-out visitor, while [mvs_dashboard], [mvs_upload] and [mvs_profile_edit] show a Log in prompt.

Low confidence, not reproducible. After deleting four items the My Media sidebar showed Media 10 on /my-media/albums/ while the database and /my-media/ showed 6; later upload/delete cycles were correct.
The Edit modal never had an allow_download control (runbook drift). Original note: no allow_download control although the REST route and the runbook contract expect it.
The Public option appears twice in the DOM (values public, public, members, followers, private); the first is a hidden placeholder option, not visible to the member.
